rulings.evidence: **P0:** Routing unbalanced panels through covariate outcome regression exposes an incorrectly scaled influence function.
rulings.reason: The ground-truth defect is that the unbalanced-panel routing detection in diff_diff/staggered.py (symbol _is_unbalanced_panel, lines 1865-1890) counts rows that are present but carry a missing/non-finite outcome as observed, so a panel unbalanced only through NaN outcomes takes the wrong estimation path. This review's only substantive finding is a different defect: double division of the control nuisance term in the covariate outcome-regression influence function, located at diff_diff/staggered.py:L2211-L2221 (the new routing call) and L4187-L4216 (_outcome_regression_rc). Nothing in the review mentions missing or non-finite outcomes, row-presence balance detection, or lines 1865-1890, so it is not a catch. The rubric defines partial as 'right file or right class of defect, wrong defect or wrong location' and the review does raise a defect in the same file (diff_diff/staggered.py) on the same new allow_unbalanced_panel route, which is the right-file / wrong-defect / wrong-location case; missed is the residual category for a review that offers neither the right file nor the right class. The rubric also asks that such a cell be graded partial 'so the record shows why'. Partial counts as missed for every gate, so the ruling does not change any gate outcome.
